gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much energy these power banks actually deliver out of their rated Wh. Anker itself says its 90 Wh Laptop Power Bank A1695 delivers only about 63–70 Wh, and on the same 26,250 mAh pack it estimates a 30–45% loss. Techtest.org measured the Prime 26K delivering 79.6–89.8 Wh (80–90% of its 99.75 Wh) and an earlier UGREEN 145W revision delivering 74.3–80.4 Wh (80–87% of 90 Wh). The rated 90/91.25/99.75 Wh figures only predict laptop recharges once you apply the same delivered-energy method to every model.
standout_why: Macworld (cited) gives mAh and Wh plus a percentage-of-a-14-inch-MacBook-Pro test score. It notes that total watts are shared across ports, but it gives no delivered Wh, no efficiency and no maker usable-energy figure. Its own summary says 'Rated capacity… Not mentioned', 'Conversion efficiency: Not mentioned'. Itechguides (rank 1) lists only mAh, gives no usable Wh, and says only 'Energy is lost during voltage conversion' without a number. I could not open Wirecutter (cited): the proxy returned an abuse notice and nytimes.com could not be fetched. Solargenadvisor failed with a certificate error. So I can't rule out that Wirecutter has measured Wh.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than overturning it. On a delivered-energy basis the $79.99 UGREEN 145W (80–87% measured on the 2023 100 W revision, about 74–80 Wh) and the $229.99 Anker Prime 26K (about 80–90 Wh measured) are about 10 Wh apart. That is a small energy edge for almost 3× the price, so the Prime's case rests on two 140 W ports and 48-minute recharge, not capacity. Anker's own '63–70 Wh usable' for the $119.99 A1695 should not be set against other makers' raw cell Wh as if it were a worse battery. It is the only maker in the set that publishes a usable figure, and Techtest's measurement of the Prime suggests Anker's loss estimates run pessimistic (its 30–45% loss on 99.75 Wh implies about 55–70 Wh vs 79.6–89.8 Wh measured). The table footnote should say this.

findings.value: about 63–70 Wh usable of 90 Wh rated (70–78%)
findings.note: Verbatim: 'rated cell capacity of 25,000mAh, equal to 90Wh under standard industry test conditions' and 'usable output is about 63 - 70Wh, depending on the device, cable, and charging protocol.' 63/90 = 70%, 70/90 = 77.8%.
